title: Cognitive Services Overview
description: Learn about Azure Cognitive Services and how pre-built vision, speech, language, and decision APIs let you add AI capabilities to any application without training models.

data.text: Azure Cognitive Services are a set of pre-built APIs that let you add artificial intelligence features to your applications without being a data scientist. Instead of collecting data, training models, and managing infrastructure, you call a simple API endpoint. Microsoft hosts the models and keeps them up to date. You pay for what you use, and you can start with a free tier for testing.

data.title: No Machine Learning Experience Required
data.text: Cognitive Services are designed for developers. You do not need to understand neural networks or training loops. If you can make an HTTP request, you can add AI to your app.

data.title: Service Categories
items: Vision: analyze images, detect objects, read text, and recognize faces.
Speech: convert speech to text, text to speech, and translate spoken languages.
Language: understand text sentiment, extract key phrases, translate documents, and build question-answering bots.
Decision: personalize recommendations, detect anomalies, and moderate content.

rows: Describe images, tag objects, and read printed text.
Detect faces, emotions, and facial landmarks.
Extract data from invoices, receipts, and forms.
Transcribe spoken audio into written text.
Convert written text into natural-sounding speech.
Translate spoken phrases in real time.
Detect sentiment, extract key phrases, and recognize language.
Turn FAQ documents into a question-answering bot.
Recommend content based on user behavior.
Identify unusual patterns in time series data.
Flag offensive text, images, or videos automatically.

data.text: Each Cognitive Service is independent. You only pay for the services you use. For example, if your app needs to read text from images and translate documents, you can subscribe to Computer Vision and Translator without using Speech or Decision APIs. This makes Cognitive Services a low-risk way to experiment with AI features before investing in custom models.

terms.definition: A collection of pre-built AI APIs on Azure that add vision, speech, language, and decision capabilities to applications.
An architectural style for building APIs that use standard HTTP methods. Most Cognitive Services expose REST endpoints.
A limited free quota for testing a service before moving to a paid tier.
The unique URL that your application calls to reach a Cognitive Service resource.

data.title: Explore the Cognitive Services Catalog
data.description: Review the full list of Cognitive Services and identify one Vision and one Speech API that could solve a problem at your workplace or in a hobby project.
steps: Open the Azure Cognitive Services product page.
Browse the Vision and Speech service categories.
Choose one Vision API and read its documentation overview.
Choose one Speech API and read its documentation overview.
Write a two-sentence summary of how you would use each API in a sample application.
data.expectedOutcome: You can name specific Cognitive Services for vision and speech tasks and explain what input they expect and what output they return.

data.title: Cognitive Services at a Glance
points: Cognitive Services offer pre-built AI APIs that require no model training.
Services are grouped into Vision, Speech, Language, and Decision categories.
You only subscribe to the APIs you need and pay per use.
Free tiers let you experiment with production-quality AI before spending money.
data.takeaway: Cognitive Services are the fastest way to add proven AI capabilities to an application without hiring a data science team.
